I renamed all projects and solution from `Ray.Automerge.xxx` to `Six.Automerge.xx`.

- Rename all namespaces in the solution from `Ray.Automerge.xxx.xxx` to `Six.Automerge.xxx.xxx`
- Rename all Rust native projects, namespaces, etc. from Ray (ray) to Six (six)
- Rename all output artefacts (that scripts produce) to:
  - from libray_automerge.so to libsix_automerge.so
  - from ray_automerge.so to libsix_automerge.dll (not that we are adding lib also on Windows to avoid special cases in naming)

- Update documentation in docs/ to use Six instead everywhere
- Update README.md
- Update CLAUDE.md
- Update everywhere where ray is mentioned to six

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
    <PropertyGroup>
        <AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks>
        <Description>Low-level P/Invoke bindings for the Automerge native library generated via Interoptopus.</Description>
        <RootNamespace>Six.Automerge.FFI</RootNamespace>
    </PropertyGroup>

    <PropertyGroup>
        <!-- Path to orchestrated Rust build script -->
        <RustBuildScript>$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)/../../scripts/build-ray-automerge-ffi.cs</RustBuildScript>
    </PropertyGroup>

    <Target Name="RunRustBuild" BeforeTargets="Compile" Condition="'$(DesignTimeBuild)' != 'true' and Exists('$(RustBuildScript)')">
        <PropertyGroup>
            <RustResolvedOutDir>$([System.String]::Copy('$(TargetDir)').Replace('\','/'))</RustResolvedOutDir>
        </PropertyGroup>
        <Message Text="Invoking Rust build script: $(RustBuildScript)" Importance="low"/>
        <Exec Command="dotnet "$(RustBuildScript)" -- --project "$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)" --out-dir "$(RustResolvedOutDir)" --configuration $(Configuration)" WorkingDirectory="$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)"/>
    </Target>

    <Target Name="ExposeNativeLibraries" DependsOnTargets="RunRustBuild" AfterTargets="Build" Condition="'$(DesignTimeBuild)' != 'true'">
        <ItemGroup>
            <NativeOutputs Include="$(OutDir)ray_automerge.dll" Condition="Exists('$(OutDir)ray_automerge.dll')">
                <TargetPath>ray_automerge.dll</TargetPath>
            </NativeOutputs>
            <NativeOutputs Include="$(OutDir)libray_automerge.so" Condition="Exists('$(OutDir)libray_automerge.so')">
                <TargetPath>libray_automerge.so</TargetPath>
            </NativeOutputs>
            <NativeOutputs Include="$(OutDir)libray_automerge.dylib" Condition="Exists('$(OutDir)libray_automerge.dylib')">
                <TargetPath>libray_automerge.dylib</TargetPath>
            </NativeOutputs>
        </ItemGroup>
        <ItemGroup>
            <ReferenceCopyLocalPaths Include="@(NativeOutputs)"/>
            <ContentWithTargetPath Include="@(NativeOutputs)">
                <CopyToOutputDirectory>PreserveNewest</CopyToOutputDirectory>
            </ContentWithTargetPath>
        </ItemGroup>
    </Target>

    <ItemGroup>
        <None Include="$(TargetDir)libray_automerge.so" Condition="Exists('$(TargetDir)libray_automerge.so')">
            <Visible>false</Visible>
            <CopyToOutputDirectory>PreserveNewest</CopyToOutputDirectory>
        </None>
        <None Include="$(TargetDir)ray_automerge.dll" Condition="Exists('$(TargetDir)ray_automerge.dll')">
            <Visible>false</Visible>
            <CopyToOutputDirectory>PreserveNewest</CopyToOutputDirectory>

            <Visible>false</Visible>
            <CopyToOutputDirectory>PreserveNewest</CopyToOutputDirectory>
        </None>
    </ItemGroup>
</Project>

<Project>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
        <LangVersion>14</LangVersion>
        <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
        <Nullable>enable</Nullable>

        <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
        <WarningsAsErrors>nullable</WarningsAsErrors>
        <NoWarn>CS1591;NU1900</NoWarn>
        <WarningsNotAsErrors>CS1723,CS0649,CS0169,CA1050,CA1822,CA2211,IDE1006,CS1574,CS1584,CS1581,CS1580,NU5104,NU1900</WarningsNotAsErrors>

        <!--
            Offline development requires restores to succeed even when public feeds are unreachable.
            These properties mirror invoking the CLI with the ignore-failed-sources switch and avoid
            repeated retries across feeds that would otherwise fail in air-gapped environments.
        -->
        <RestoreIgnoreFailedSources>true</RestoreIgnoreFailedSources>
        <RestoreDisableParallel>true</RestoreDisableParallel>
    </PropertyGroup>

    <ItemGroup>
        <PackageReference Include="JetBrains.Annotations" Version="2025.2.4"/>
    </ItemGroup>

    <!--        
        StyleCop: https://github.com/DotNetAnalyzers/StyleCopAnalyzers
    -->
    <PropertyGroup>
        <CodeAnalysisRuleSet>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory).ruleset</CodeAnalysisRuleSet>
        <StyleCopTreatErrorsAsWarnings>false</StyleCopTreatErrorsAsWarnings>
        <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
        <AnalysisLevel>preview</AnalysisLevel>
    </PropertyGroup>

    <ItemGroup>
        <AdditionalFiles Include="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)stylecop.json" Link="stylecop.json"/>
    </ItemGroup>


    <!-- CI/CD Build Optimization -->
    <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Release'">
        <!-- CI-specific optimizations -->
        <ContinuousIntegrationBuild Condition="'$(CI)' == 'true' or '$(GITHUB_ACTIONS)' == 'true' or '$(TF_BUILD)' == 'true'">true</ContinuousIntegrationBuild>

        <!-- Deterministic builds for reproducibility -->
        <Deterministic>true</Deterministic>
        <DeterministicSourcePaths>true</DeterministicSourcePaths>

        <!-- Disable features not needed in CI -->
        <UseSharedCompilation>false</UseSharedCompilation>
        <DisableImplicitNuGetFallbackFolder>true</DisableImplicitNuGetFallbackFolder>
    </PropertyGroup>

</Project>

# Ray.Toolkit.Automerge.FFI Build Configuration

## Platform-Specific Build Targets

To avoid cross-platform Rust artifact conflicts when building on different operating systems or in WSL, this project uses platform-specific target directories for the Rust codegen.

### Automatic Platform Detection

The build system automatically detects your platform and uses the appropriate target directory:

| Platform | Detection | Target Directory |
|----------|-----------|------------------|
| **Windows** | `$(OS) == 'Windows_NT'` | `codegen/target-windows` |
| **Linux** | `uname -s` == `Linux` | `codegen/target-linux` |
| **macOS** | `uname -s` == `Darwin` | `codegen/target-macos` |
| **Other Unix** | Fallback | `codegen/target-unix` |

### How It Works

1. **DetectPlatform Target**: Runs `uname -s` on Unix systems to distinguish Linux from macOS
2. **BuildNative Target**: Compiles the Rust native library
3. **GenerateInterop Target**: Runs the Rust codegen using the platform-specific target directory

### Building

Simply run:
```bash
dotnet build Ray.Automerge.FFI.csproj
```

The build will automatically:
- Detect your platform
- Use the correct target directory
- Build the native Rust library
- Generate C# interop code via Interoptopus

### WASM Support

For WebAssembly builds, you would need a separate build configuration:

1. Install wasm-pack: `cargo install wasm-pack`
2. Build with: `wasm-pack build --target web` (or other targets)
3. This would require separate MSBuild targets or a dedicated build script

WASM builds are not included in the standard dotnet build process as they target a completely different runtime environment.

### Troubleshooting

**Issue**: Build fails with "couldn't find crate with expected target triple"

**Solution**: This occurs when switching between Windows and WSL builds. The platform-specific directories should prevent this, but if you encounter it:

```bash
# Manually clean codegen artifacts
cd libs/Ray.Toolkit.Automerge.FFI/codegen
cargo clean --manifest-path=Cargo.toml
```

**Issue**: Platform not detected correctly

**Solution**: The build will output: `Detected platform: <name>, using target directory: <path>`.
Check this message to verify detection. If incorrect, you can manually set `CodegenTargetDir`:

```bash
dotnet build /p:CodegenTargetDir="libs/Ray.Toolkit.Automerge.FFI/codegen/target-custom"
```

### Build Artifacts

All platform-specific directories are gitignored:
- `target-windows/`
- `target-linux/`
- `target-macos/`
- `target-unix/`
- `target-wasm/`

This allows developers to work on multiple platforms without conflicts in version control.

## 🚀 What is Ray.Automerge?

**Ray.Automerge** are production-ready C# bindings for a Rust-based library [Automerge](https://github.
com/automerge/automerge) that make it easy to build collaborative applications using CRDT structures.


## AI Agent Reference for creating FFI Code and Bindings

- Use (Interoptopus)[https://github.com/ralfbiedert/interoptopus] to generate C# bindings for the Rust library.
- Use the `.externs/interoptopus/examples/real_project_layout/` directory as an example usage how to prepare and create Rust bindings for C#.


## 🏗️ Project Structure

```
Ray.Automerge/                                  # Root directory of the solution
├── apps/                                       # Application projects
│   └── DemoApp.Basic/                          # Demo application demonstrating the Automerge features in C#
├── libs/                                       # Library projects
│   └── Ray.Automerge/                          # C# bindings for the Automerge Rust library
│   └── Ray.Automerge.FFI/                      # Rust FFI code for the Automerge and low level C# library
│       ├── src/                                # Low-level C# library with direct bindings to Rust FFI code
│       └── native/                             # Rust FFI code
├── tests/                                      # Test projects
│   └── Ray.Automerge.FFI.Test.Unit/            # Unit tests for the C# low level library
├── scripts/                                    # C# build scripts (requires .NET 10)
│   ├── pack.cs                                 # NuGet packaging script
│   ├── tests-run.cs                            # Test execution script
│   ├── tests-coverage.cs                       # Coverage collection script
│   └── tests-report.cs                         # Coverage reporting script
├── docs/                                       # In-Repository Astro.js/Starlight documentation site
├── .references/                                # Directories with Rust source files of Automerge; for AI agent reference to be able to see the native APIs when writing FFI code and bindings.
├── .github/                                    # GitHub workflows and templates
└── Configuration files                         # Global project settings in the solution root (global.json, nuget.config, .editorconfig, etc.)
```


## 🛠️ Prerequisites

- **.NET 10 SDK**: Required for C# file-based apps (build scripts)
- **pnpm/npm**: For documentation site build


### Key Components
- **Application Projects**: Located in `apps/` directory
- **Library Projects**: Located in `libs/` directory
- **Test Projects**: Located in `tests/` directory
- **Build Scripts**: **C# file-based apps** in `scripts/` directory (requires .NET 10)
- **Documentation**: **Astro.js** Starlight site in `docs/` directory
- **CI/CD**: GitHub Actions workflows in `.github/workflows/`

## ✨ Key Features

### 🎯 **Project Structure & Configuration**
- **Global .NET Version Management**: Configured with .NET 10 (.NET 10.0.100-rc.1 currently) in `global.json`
- **Language Features**: C# 13, nullable reference types, implicit usings enabled
- **Directory Organization**: Clear separation of `apps/`, `libs/`, `tests/`, and `benchmarks/` projects

### 🔧 **Code Quality & Standards**
- **StyleCop Integration**: Automated code style enforcement with `stylecop.json`
- **EditorConfig**: Consistent coding standards across all IDEs
- **Code Analysis**: Built-in rule sets and analysis configuration
- **Treat Warnings as Errors**: Ensures high code quality standards

### 📦 **NuGet Package Management**
- **Environment-Based Configuration**: Support for local, development, staging, and public NuGet feeds
- **Automated Publishing**: C# scripts for packaging and publishing (requires .NET 10)
- **Package Metadata**: Centralized package configuration in `Directory.Build.props`

### 🧪 **Testing & Quality Assurance**
- **C# Scripts**: File-based apps for testing workflows (requires .NET 10)
- **Code Coverage**: Automated coverage collection and reporting

### 📚 **Documentation & Publishing**
- **Astro.js Starlight**: Modern documentation site with **Six theme**
- **GitHub Pages**: Automatic deployment **on push to main branch**
- **Beautiful & Modern Theme**: With Six theme; clean, modern, and responsive design
- **Search & Navigation**: Full-text search and organized navigation

### 🧩 **FFI Regeneration & Build Workflow**
- **Regenerate bindings:** `cargo run --offline --manifest-path libs/Ray.Toolkit.Automerge.FFI/codegen/Cargo.toml`
- **Build native library:** `cargo build --release --offline --manifest-path libs/Ray.Toolkit.Automerge.FFI/native/Cargo.toml`
- **Managed build:** `dotnet build` (invokes the steps above automatically inside `Ray.Toolkit.Automerge.FFI.csproj`)
- **Offline note:** If NuGet feeds are unavailable, add `NU1900` to `WarningsNotAsErrors` (already configured) or temporarily pass `--ignore-failed-sources` during restore.


----
